evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/utils/imageCompression.ts:171 (compressImagesIfNeeded) — the down-scale pass calls manipulateAsync(uri, [{ resize: { width: maxDimension } }], ...) with ONLY a width bound. expo-image-manipulator's width-only resize sets width to 1920 and scales height by aspect ratio, so for PORTRAIT photos (the dominant phone-camera orientation) it caps the SHORTER edge and leaves the longest edge (height) uncapped — a 3000x4000 shot becomes 1920x2560 (longest edge 2560, not 1920).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/utils/imageCompression.ts:12-15 and :118 — the doc comment states the strategy is to 'cap the longest edge at MAX_DIMENSION px', which diverges from the width-only implementation: the stated intent is not met for portrait images.

Consequence: portrait images narrower than 1920px are UPSCALED by the resize op (larger target width => more pixels), which can increase byte size and works against the 10 MB reduction goal of AC 4.1 (Story 4.1 / issue #1767). The correct recipe bounds both edges (e.g. resize by width only when landscape and by height only when portrait, or pass the longest-edge dimension per orientation).

Reachable in production: compressImagesIfNeeded is the offline fault-report photo path (ReportFaultScreen). Net-new — prior mobile-rn passes (incl. 2026-08-08, which only credited the module with 'having tests') never flagged the resize logic; imageCompression.test.ts:115 pins the shipped call shape as { resize: { width: 1920 } }, so a fix must update that assertion too.
